newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian refugees protest against UN in Slavonia.
newsitem.headline: Croatian refugees protest against UN in Slavonia.

text.p: Several thousand Croatian refugees rallied in two eastern towns on Friday demanding the end of the U.N. mission in the country's last Serb-held enclave by January 15, Croatian media reported.

"Gentlemen...time is up, and we have to go back to our land which is at the moment under (Serb) occupation," state news agency Hina quoted the head of the Croatian refugee association, Mato Simic, as telling 7,000 people gathered in the town of Vinkovci.
The U.N. Transitional Authority in Eastern Slavonia (UNTAES) used its 5,000 peacekeeping troops to take over the area in January to prepare it for reintegration into Croatia.
It has has been given a one-year mandate which can be extended up to a year if difficulties arise.
The UNTAES mandate includes demilitarisation, economic rehabilitation, reconstruction and the return of Croatian refugees.
Eastern Slavonia was one of three Serb-held regions in Croatia which rebelled against Zagreb's bid for independence from old Yugoslavia.
The Croatian army recaptured two other separatist enclaves in a series of blitz offensives in 1995, leading to a mass exodus of the Serb population.
Last month U.N. Secretary General Boutros Boutros Ghali recommended that UNTAES should stay in Eastern Slavonia for another year. Croatia has so far agreed to extend the madate by only three months.
Croatian television HRT said refugees were bitter that UNTAES had not returned any of them to their homes so far.
In his speech to the refugees, Simic said they could not allow the U.N. administration to stay for one more year.
"We can wait until January 15. But (on that day) we want president Franjo Tudjman to lead us to Vukovar," Simic told the rally.
Vukovar, the scene of Yugoslav conflict's worst destruction, fell to Serb militia and the Yugoslav army in November 1991. Almost all non-Serbs were then expelled.
HRT said another 8,000 refugees held a similar rally in Osijek on the border with Eastern Slavonia.
